transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam Torres (Redwood CSM), Marcus Hale (Celestia Legal Ops), Sofia Ortega (Head of IT), David Lin (Procurement), Emily Park (Security)

Summary: Short procurement/contract discussion focused on MSA redlines, DPA data residency, SLA targets (99.9% uptime, p99 latency), pricing discounts tied to committed usage, and next steps for vendor onboarding and pilot. Agreed to legal-only sync and Redwood to send redlined documents + SE benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick roll call — alex here on the AE side, priya is our SE, liam from CSM. Marcus you good?
[00:08] Marcus Hale: Yep Marcus on the call, thanks. We have Sofia and David and Emily as well.
[00:13] Sofia Ortega: Hi, thanks.
[00:14] Priya Kapoor: Hi all. Quick agenda — MSA redlines, DPA specifics around residency and encryption, SLA numbers we can guarantee, pricing and timelines to get the pilot live.
[00:25] David Lin: Sounds good. Procurement just wants to know the timeline — we'll need an approved vendor packet and pricing sheet before we can route a PO.
[00:31] Alex Chen: Understood - we'll include the vendor packet. On MSA, Marcus you sent the redlines earlier, we skimmed them and there are three big asks — indemnity caps, data residency addition in the DPA, and a 60 day termination for convenience clause that you flagged.
[00:44] Marcus Hale: Right, we want to limit liability to direct damages and carve out punitive, and shift some of the IP warranty language. Also we asked for an explicit audit rights paragraph which I think was missing.
[00:55] Alex Chen: Cool. Priya, do you want to speak to any technical constraints that affect DPA language, like where data sits during inference?
[01:02] Priya Kapoor: Sure. For hosted we route to our Redwood API — which abides by default retention policies — but for the enterprise Dedicated or Private deployment we can absolutely limit persistence. Just note that sometimes folks refer to our KV cache as "KV cash" in notes — but it's just ephemeral unless you enable prefix caching.
[01:22] Emily Park: For us, the main ask is that PHI-like identifiers are never persisted outside the EU region. We also need keys in our KMS, not Redwood-managed keys.
[01:31] Priya Kapoor: That's doable — we support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated; the only nuance is with hosted where BYOK isn't available today. I'll flag the exact product names — Redwood Privatee (sic) is the on-prem bundle — our docs sometimes shorthand it.
[01:51] Sofia Ortega: Can you confirm SOC 2 and pen test reports?
[01:54] Liam Torres: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and the latest pen test summary; full reports are provided under NDA if needed.
[02:03] Marcus Hale: About SLAs, procurement needs to see uptime and p99 latency targets — and what credits look like if breached.
[02:10] Alex Chen: Our standard SLA for Dedicated is 99.9% uptime and we commit to p99 latency targets that vary by model and config. For enterprise deals we can contract specific p99 numbers, e.g., 200ms p99 for small seq lengths — but we'll need to benchmark with your workload. Credits are typically service credits tiered based on duration of degradation.
[02:28] David Lin: Will that be spelled out in the SOW or the SLA addendum? Procurement prefers an SLA addendum.
[02:33] Alex Chen: SLA addendum is fine — we'll include specific metrics and the remediation steps. Priya, can you run the workload benchmark?
[02:38] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we'll need sample prompts, expected concurrency, and target seq length. If you can share a small dataset we can run a 24-48 hour benchmark and produce p50/p95/p99 numbers and a runbook for the pilot.
[02:51] Marcus Hale: For the DPA, we added a clause about data residency and deletion timelines — 30 days for deletion unless under legal hold. Is that compatible?
[02:58] Priya Kapoor: 30 days is standard for Hosted where caches may take some time to evict; for Dedicated/Private we can do same-day or configurable policies depending on persistence settings. There is sometimes replication lag for cross-region backups.
[03:16] Emily Park: Also need to confirm key rotation and HSM support.
[03:19] Priya Kapoor: We integrate with customer KMS — HSM-backed keys supported via AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS depending on region. We'll document the key rotation procedures in the onboarding packet.
[03:31] Marcus Hale: On the MSA front, our counsel wants changes to limitation of liability and indemnity when it comes to IP claims — they'd like vendor to be on the hook for third-party IP claims. What's Redwood's position?
[03:42] Alex Chen: We can discuss once we see the redline. We generally have a mutual indemnity for IP infringement, with caps tied to fees paid, but enterprise exceptions can be negotiated. I'll highlight where we can flex and where we need to keep company policy.
[03:54] Marcus Hale: Ok please call those out in the redline.
[03:57] Alex Chen: Will do. David, around pricing — are you looking for committed monthly spend with a discount, or a pilot-rate?
[04:05] David Lin: Procurement prefers a committed discount tier, because it simplifies approvals. But we need a pilot number to justify the commitment.
[04:12] Alex Chen: Typical flow: pilot at a reduced rate or credits, then a committed monthly commitment for dedicated pool with a discount on per-token and embedding units. We'll send a pricing sheet with tiered discounts and breakpoints.
[04:25] Sofia Ortega: What about termination and exit data export? We need a clean data export path and guarantee deletion after termination.
[04:32] Priya Kapoor: We'll provide an export utility and an exit checklist; for Dedicated/Private you get direct access. For Hosted we'll provide an export within the DPA timeframes and certify deletion. Note sometimes our auto-transcribe mislabels names — please assume the artifact links we send are accurate.
[04:50] Marcus Hale: Also want audit logs and SSO — we use Okta SAML today.
[04:54] Alex Chen: We support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning on enterprise plans. Audit logs are included on the enterprise observability addon — we'll include a sample retention policy.
[05:04] Emily Park: Any export controls or data crossing borders we should be aware of?
[05:08] Priya Kapoor: We can pin region routing — smart routing can be set to not cross EU boundaries for requests originating in EU. There are nuances with third-party integrations, we'll call those out.
[05:18] Marcus Hale: Good. Let's talk timelines — if we get a redline and you send the SOC2 and pricing, we can aim to have procurement approval within two weeks? David?
[05:26] David Lin: If legal approves the redline quickly and pricing is in line, two weeks is realistic from our side to approve the vendor and issue PO.
[05:33] Alex Chen: Great. For the pilot, do you want us to propose a scope? Priya can outline a 3-week pilot with specific acceptance criteria.
[05:40] Sofia Ortega: Yes, a short pilot with success metrics like p99 < 300ms for 8 worker concurrency and accuracy checks on outputs.
[05:47] Priya Kapoor: We'll draft a pilot SOW: dataset, expected QPS, sequence length, acceptance criteria (latency, throughput, and qualitative checks).
[05:56] Marcus Hale: Are there any legal items that are typically non-negotiable?
[05:59] Alex Chen: Usually export control, sanctions, and compliance with law are standard clauses. We are conservative on unlimited indemnity asks and certain IP carve-outs. We'll flag anything we can't change and offer alternative wording.
[06:11] Marcus Hale: Ok. Also please provide a template SLA addendum with credits formula.
[06:16] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll include SLA addendum + example credits ladder.
[06:20] David Lin: One more — do you have a list of subcontractors or cloud providers? We need to add them to our vendor list.
[06:25] Liam Torres: We'll provide a subcontractor list and a network diagram.
[06:30] Marcus Hale: Great. That about covers it, any other items?
[06:33] Sofia Ortega: Just onboarding — how long to stand up Dedicated versus Hosted pilot?
[06:37] Priya Kapoor: Hosted pilot is fastest — can be minutes to hours; Dedicated requires provisioning and typically 2-3 weeks depending on capacity and region. Private on-prem can be 6-8 weeks. We'll include a timeline matrix in the onboarding packet.
[06:52] Marcus Hale: Can you also include a sample SOW for the pilot cost estimate?
[06:56] Alex Chen: Absolutely. We'll include a sample SOW and cost estimate with the pricing sheet.
[07:01] Marcus Hale: Ok last thing — security review hurdles. Emily, do you want to summarize?
[07:05] Emily Park: We need SOC2, pen test, encryption at rest and in transit, customer-managed KMS for PHI, and a vulnerability response SLA. If those are covered we can proceed to procurement.
[07:18] Alex Chen: We'll send the artifacts and a vulnerability response SLA.
[07:21] Marcus Hale: Thanks. Let's recap next steps — Alex to email redlined MSA/DPA and pricing; Priya to run the benchmark; schedule legal sync next week.
[07:31] Alex Chen: Yep, I'll follow up with a calendar invite. Appreciate everyone's time.
[07:36] David Lin: Thanks all.
[07:38] Sofia Ortega: Thanks.
[07:39] Priya Kapoor: Bye.

End transcript.
